pass_condition: Every D-TIE-1 level compares the same way in SQL as in cvi.core.tiebreak.tie_key.

findings.statement: Tie level 7 compares last_human_commit_at as TEXT in SQL but as an epoch in Python, so any commit date carrying a non-Z UTC offset orders differently in the two paths.
findings.failure_scenario: Two rows tied through level 6, dated '2026-01-01T20:00:00-05:00' (the later instant) and '2026-01-02T00:00:00Z': assign_ranks puts the offset-bearing row first, ranked_order_sql puts it second -- python ['earlier_text_later_instant', ...] vs sql ['later_text_earlier_instant', ...], PARITY: False.

observations: Latent today: no producer supplies last_non_bot_commit_at yet (cvi.core.tiebreak's own docstring says every caller passes None), which is exactly why it needs pinning before one does.
This is the same defect class as W2-6 round 1's Blocker, closed on the Python side and still open on the SQL side.
Fix: normalise the column to UTC 'Z' on write (or store an epoch) and add a mixed-offset row to the parity fixture.
Separately: SQLite ROUND(82.125,2)=82.13 while Python round(82.125,2)=82.12; inert today because the engine rounds once to 2 dp before the store sees the value.
